steps.find: a blue letter waits in your mailbox
steps.away: a blue letter waits in your mailbox at home

steps.find: nib waits at the town hall in banana town
steps.note: Nib’s spare lantern, for after dark

lines.text: You came. Thank you. I have not slept properly since it started.
Here is Plot 11’s page. Look just above the scratch.
Plot 11
Someone is writing the name back in.
One letter every night. I lock the hall at dusk, and I hold the only key.
So who is writing them?
I do not know. But this morning the newest letter was still wet.
And it did not stay on the page. It dripped out of the book, across my floor and under the door.
I could not make myself follow it. The drops are still out there on the cobbles.
I’ll follow them.
Thank you. Take my spare lantern. I would feel better knowing you have a light.

steps.find: follow the ink drops from the town hall door
the ink leads to the statue by the town hall

lines.text: TOO BIG. G.F.
Four screw holes, and a clean square where something used to hang.
Someone signed the chalk with a G and an F.

steps.find: g.f. is gran fig. find her in the west garden
steps.note: a fig, and orders to eat it

lines.text: Stop staring at my beds. You were at the statue. I saw.
It had a plaque once.
Of course it had a plaque. Every statue has a plaque. Do not be slow.
It was a fountain too. Water from the jug, all day long. Then one night it stopped, and nobody fixed it. Poor work.
The chalk is mine. I measure that statue whenever I cross the square. Too much stone for a nobody.
I write to the Mayor every week: take it down. It makes me sad and I do not know why. I do not like not knowing why.
Brass does not walk off. If it left this square, it went by post. Ask Stamp at the post office. Now.

steps.find: find stamp at the post office

lines.text: Gran Fig sent you. She sends everyone. Noted.
Did anybody ever post a brass plaque?
One parcel I never delivered. It was on the bottom shelf when I came. Posted in 1999, from the Town Hall, to Plot 11.
No name for Plot 11 in the big book. Nobody to hand it to. It has sat there since.
You live on Plot 11 now. It is yours. Two kilos, and heavy for its size.
Somebody scraped the front clean off.
for teaching us all the dance
So the statue was for whoever taught everyone to dance.
The label is in the Town Hall’s own hand. Very neat letters.
Moss sweeps past that statue every morning. Ask her. Noted.

steps.find: find moss by the fountain in the square
steps.note: the oldest flyer in Banana Town

lines.text: The statue. Yes. I sweep past it every morning, and I have never once seen water in it.
Gran Fig says it stopped one night.
One night, yes. The same night the ghosts first came, and they have come back every night since.
Always the same. They break what we fix, and I thought it was spite, but now I think they are looking for something.
Looking for what?
Not sure. This was under the floor of my room when I came. The oldest flyer I own.
DANCE NIGHT on the eleventh plot. Everyone welcome. You will know the steps by the end. Hosted by
The host’s name is torn off.
Torn off. The whole town went that night, and not one of us remembers going.
That must be where everyone learned the dance.
Must be. My feet know every step, and I cannot remember learning one.

steps.find: bring the plaque and the flyer to nib

lines.text: A plaque with the name scraped off. A flyer with the name torn off.
And my book, with the name scratched out. Three of them. Somebody was very thorough.
Let me look at the page properly. I owe it that.
Two little dots, right where the scratch begins.
Before I write any name, I set my pen at the edge of the page and tap it twice. Every name, since the day I came.
Those are my taps. I did this. And I do not remember doing it.

steps.find: nib has more to show you at the town hall

lines.text: The Mayor has never spoken to me. Notes come under the door instead. I keep every one, in order.
This is the oldest. 1999.
take the eleventh name out of the book tonight. it is the only way to keep them safe. then forget you did. — M.
And I did. Both parts.
This is the newest. It came a week before you did.
somebody is coming for the eleventh plot. be kind to them. — M.
That was me.
That was you. The rumour I told you about was this note, under my door.
There is a line in the book for my family. I have always left it empty.
I could not bear to invent a name. And I always hoped one might arrive.
One is arriving, a letter at a time.
Yes. Keep the newest note. It was always about you.
Tonight, then. At the book. Come back when the square goes dark.

steps.find: when the moon clock runs out, meet nib at the town hall
steps.away: at nightfall, meet nib at the town hall in banana town
steps.nightfall: night has fallen. nib waits at the town hall

lines.text: You brought the lantern. Good.
There. By the door. It has come for the book.
The page is glowing.
It is finished. The whole name.
Water runs from the statue again.
Oh. Oh, I know you. You are my—
No. No, no. I had it. I had it just now.
The light over the door just went out.
That is the Mayor’s window.
Go home, resident. Please. Go home and lock the door.

steps.away: go home. something waits in your mailbox
steps.note: a black letter with no stamp
